purpose: This medication is used to prevent and control seizures. It is commonly prescribed for epilepsy and certain types of seizure disorders. It may also be used after brain surgery to help prevent seizures.
how_it_works: Your brain sends electrical signals between nerve cells, and sometimes those signals go haywire and cause a seizure. Phenytoin works by calming down those overactive electrical signals in the brain. Think of it like a circuit breaker that keeps the electricity in your brain from going into overdrive.
common_side_effects: You might notice dizziness, drowsiness, or feeling unsteady on your feet. Some people experience nausea, vomiting, or constipation. Overgrowth of the gums, unusual hair growth on the body, and slurred speech can also occur. Your vision may seem blurry or you might see double, especially when starting the medication.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can trigger serious seizures. This drug can affect your liver, blood counts, and can cause a serious skin rash — contact your doctor right away if you develop a rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual bruising. It can interact with many other medications and can harm an unborn baby, so tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Regular blood tests are needed to make sure you have the right amount of medicine in your body.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 300 mg taken once daily, or sometimes split into smaller doses. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on blood level tests to find the right amount for you. Always take it at the same time each day and swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or chew them.
